Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: Japan, with implications for US, Europe, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Japan's 10-year JGB yield hit 3% for the first time since 1996, triggering a broad global bond selloff. The move is driven by a confluence of BOJ rate-hike expectations, fiscal sustainability concerns, Middle East escalation pushing Brent crude above $91/bbl, and a structural shift in Japan's role as marginal buyer of foreign bonds. Analysts largely frame this as a regime change — not a crisis — with global term premium repricing upward across developed markets including the US. Fed rate hike expectations (September start, minimum 3-hike cycle) are also cited as a key driver. Spillover risks include repatriation of Japanese capital, reduced Japanese demand for foreign debt (particularly USTs), carry trade unwinding, and fiscal pressure across major sovereigns.

Relevance: NO — the primary subject is JGB yields and Japan, but US rates/Fed policy are a material secondary theme with direct cross-market implications.
